nom: d'Alba Piedmont UV Tone-Up Sunscreen Broad Spectrum SPF 50+

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin report it doesn't feel cakey or excessively greasy, with one calling it the best sunscreen she has used for her oily skin, though one general comment warns the dewy finish may look too shiny on very oily skin types.
segments.sensitive: The couple of reviewers who specify sensitive skin report no irritation and recommend it for that skin type.
segments.dry: The one reviewer specifying dry, acne-prone skin found it worked well for her through the summer.

concerns.redness: Many reviewers say the pink tone-up tint visibly reduces the look of redness and evens out complexion on contact, though for some the effect fades within about an hour; a couple of reviewers report it did not reduce their redness at all.
concerns.blemishes: A few reviewers with acne-prone skin report it doesn't cause breakouts and even helps camouflage or calm active blemishes.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily skin generally find it doesn't feel greasy or cakey, though one general comment warns the dewy finish can look too shiny on very oily skin.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers describe the formula as hydrating and moisturizing, while at least one found it made her skin look drier and more textured, and another wishes it had more moisturizing qualities.

aspects.libelle: Leaves a visible white cast, especially on fair or pale skin
Pink-violet tint can look unnatural on deeper or tan skin tones
Pleasant fragrance, not the typical sunscreen smell
Lightweight, blends smoothly and absorbs within minutes
A little goes a long way, bottle lasts a season

extraits.texte: I am pale/light skinned and this makes my face look ghostly, almost purple. It takes a lot of bronzer to bring any color back. It seems to layer well with other products but I'll be returning it.

** I received this product for free through BzzAgent** TLDR: Be cautious buying if you have a darker skin tone, otherwise product is good. I have tan skin and this sunscreen left a slight white cast on my skin no matter how much I rubbed it in and let it set, I don't use makeup but I'm sure a good foundation would do the trick at hiding it. It absorbed fully into my skin after about 5 minutes, I felt slightly oily and smelt vaguely of sunscreen but it wasn't super noticeable to friends when I asked them if it was obvious I was wearing sunscreen. I wore a patch of product on my arm and by the end of the day that patch was noticeably lighter than the rest of my skin so I'd say it does it's job (note: I did reapply a few times throughout the day).

extraits.titre: Great sunscreen, but doesn't reduce redness
extraits.texte: I really love this sunscreen. It covers well without feeling heavy or thick on my face. It also has a pleasant fragrance. I have spent longs days in the hot sun without getting burn. My only issue is that it does not reduce the redness and if anything I feel like it brightens the redness for a good hour before returning to the redness before applied.
